description: Oil level monitor (Monitor de Nível de Óleo): float level, alarm and shutdown thresholds, four relays, analog output and Modbus RTU
source: Electron do Brasil, Mapa de Registradores Modbus RTU, MNO – Monitor de Nível de Óleo, v3.0.2

sources.title: Mapa de Registradores Modbus RTU, MNO – Monitor de Nível de Óleo

notes: All registers are holding registers. The document numbers them 1 to 38 and calls the type Read Holding Register (40.000), so the addresses are 1-based (address on the wire = number minus 1). The document does not say so explicitly: if a read fails, try address_base 0.

The document allows 2400 to 57600 bps, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit and no, even or odd parity. It gives no default baud rate or slave address: 9600 N and 1 are placeholders; the slave address is in register 25.

Levels are shown in the document with one decimal and a scale of -1000:10, which it does not explain. They are given as raw values: check against the display before applying a scale. The shutdown delay has no unit in the document.

Registers 7, 9, 12, 18, 19 and 20 are bit fields, one entry per bit. The command bits are write-only. The baud rate, parity and protocol registers (22 to 24) are read-only in this document. Registers 26, 29 and 33 to 34 are not in the document.
The serial number is 48 bits in registers 35 to 37; it is given as a 16-bit register and a 32-bit one, so it has no serial role.
Written from the manufacturer's document; not tested on a device.
